chapter_title: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: Which of the following are major structural drawbacks of traditional operating system file processing systems (Select all that apply)?

options.A: Data redundancy and inconsistency across decentralized departmental files
options.B: Difficulty in accessing ad-hoc data without writing custom programs
options.C: Automatic conversion of queries into optimal relational algebra trees
options.D: Data isolation caused by disparate, incompatible file formats
options.E: Lack of fine-grained access control and atomicity guarantees during power crashes

questions.rationale: File processing systems suffer from redundancy (A), difficulty accessing data (B), isolation across formats (D), and atomicity/security deficits (E). Converting queries to relational algebra (C) is a feature of modern DBMS query optimizers, not a drawback of file systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following levels are formal tiers within the ANSI-SPARC Three-Schema Architecture (Select all that apply)?
questions.rationale: The Three-Schema Architecture defines exactly three abstraction levels: Physical (A), Conceptual/Logical (B), and External/View (C). Network Protocol (D) and Application Operating (E) are not schema abstraction levels.

questions.stem: Which of the following attributes are correctly classified as Composite Attributes (Select all that apply)?

options.C: Mailing_Address (Decomposed into Street, City, State, Pincode)

questions.rationale: Composite attributes can be divided into smaller sub-parts with independent meanings, such as Name (B), Address (C), and GPS Coordinates (E). Aadhar Number (A) is an atomic/simple attribute, and Age (D) is a derived attribute.

questions.stem: Which geometric symbols represent components of an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram in standard Chen notation (Select all that apply)?

options.E: Double Oval representing a Multivalued Attribute

questions.rationale: In Chen notation: Entity sets are rectangles (A), relationships are diamonds (B), attributes are ovals (C), and multivalued attributes are double ovals (E). Primary keys are indicated by underlined attribute text inside ovals, never hexagons (D).

questions.stem: Which of the following properties are guaranteed for transactions by the ACID model in a DBMS (Select all that apply)?

options.A: Atomicity (all operations complete successfully or none are applied)
options.C: Isolation (concurrent execution yields states equivalent to serial execution)
options.D: Durability (committed data persists across system crashes)

questions.rationale: ACID stands for Atomicity (A), Consistency (B), Isolation (C), and Durability (D). Elasticity (E) is a cloud computing infrastructure metric, not a core ACID transaction invariant.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the Relational Model are formally true (Select all that apply)?

options.A: A relation is mathematically defined as a subset of the Cartesian product of attribute domains
options.B: A tuple represents an individual row in a relation table
options.C: The order of tuples in a relation instance is strictly guaranteed by disk track sector order
options.D: Degree refers to the total number of attributes (columns) in a relation
options.E: All attribute values in First Normal Form (1NF) must be atomic

questions.rationale: Relations are mathematical sets of tuples (A), rows are tuples (B), degree is column count (D), and 1NF requires atomic values (E). Under formal set theory, tuple order is unordered (C is false).

questions.stem: Which of the following are recognized mapping cardinality ratios for binary relationships (Select all that apply)?
questions.rationale: The four standard binary mapping cardinality ratios are 1:1 (A), 1:N (B), N:1 (C), and M:N (D). Zero-to-zero (E) is not a defined cardinality ratio in database modeling.

questions.stem: Which of the following are fundamental (primitive) operators in formal Relational Algebra (Select all that apply)?
questions.rationale: Selection (A), Projection (B), Cartesian Product (C), and Set Union (D) are fundamental operators (along with Set Difference and Rename). Natural Join (E) is a derived operator synthesized from Cartesian product, selection, and projection.

questions.stem: Which components are direct functional modules of the DBMS Storage Manager (Select all that apply)?
questions.rationale: The Storage Manager comprises the Buffer Manager (A), File Manager (B), Authorization/Integrity Manager (C), and Index Manager (E). The DML Compiler (D) belongs to the Query Processor.

questions.stem: Which conditions are mandatory characteristics of a Weak Entity Set (Select all that apply)?

options.A: It lacks a primary key of its own
options.B: It must have total participation in its identifying relationship
options.C: It is visually depicted using a double rectangle in ER diagrams
options.D: It can exist in the database without an identifying owner entity
options.E: Its discriminator attribute is denoted with a dashed underline

questions.rationale: A weak entity set lacks a primary key (A), has total participation in its identifying relationship (B), uses a double rectangle (C), and has a discriminator with a dashed underline (E). It is existence-dependent and cannot exist without an owner (D is false).
